                    ### Question
                    A 6-week-old boy is brought for routine examination at his pediatrician’s office. The patient was born at 39 weeks to a 26-year-old G1P1 mother by normal vaginal delivery. External cephalic version was performed successfully at 37 weeks for breech presentation. Pregnancy was complicated by gestational diabetes that was well-controlled with insulin. The patient’s maternal grandmother has early onset osteoporosis. On physical examination, the left hip dislocates posteriorly with adduction and depression of a flexed femur. An ultrasound is obtained that reveals left acetabular dysplasia and a dislocated left femur. Which of the following is the next best step in management?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Closed reduction and spica casting
opb. Observation
opc. Open reduction and femoral osteotomy
opd. Pavlik harness
ope. Physiotherapy

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The next best step in management for the 6-week-old boy with left acetabular dysplasia and a dislocated left femur is closed reduction and spica casting. This approach is commonly used for infants under 6 months with developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) to maintain hip reduction and promote proper hip development. Observation alone may lead to worsening of hip dislocation and long-term complications. Open reduction and femoral osteotomy are reserved for severe cases or failed closed reduction. The Pavlik harness is another option for infants under 6 months with DDH. Physiotherapy may be used as an adjunct but is not typically the initial management for DDH.
